compiled_state.title: [llm-review remediation]: re-review 29 PRs merged without LLM dispatch (post-bug 1624-5fb9)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

Bug 1624-5fb9 (P0) found that the `llm-review` CI job silently skipped LLM dispatch for direct PRs to main between 2026-05-15 (commit 9a4847206b) and 2026-05-17 (fix in PR #188). 29 first-parent merges to main during this window contain code changes that were never evaluated by the configured code reviewer.

## Scope

Sampled 5/5 PRs (#171, #172, #175, #180, #186) confirm the silent-skip pattern via 'Integration scope: 0 file(s) — skipping LLM review dispatch' in the job log followed by SUCCESS with no findings. Remaining 24 share the same direct-PR flow and the gate is deterministic on that flow — they are presumptively affected.

## Remediation Approach Options

Option 1 — **Retro-review only** (lowest cost): Run the LLM reviewer offline against each merge SHA's diff, file any blocking findings as bugs against the responsible owners. Code already on main — no code revert needed unless findings are critical.

Option 2 — **Retro-review + remediation PRs**: After offline review, open follow-up PRs that fix any critical/important findings discovered. The newly-fixed llm-review job will catch those findings on the remediation PRs.

Option 3 — **Spot-check critical merges only**: Manually identify which of the 29 PRs touched safeguard / security / production-critical paths and offline-review just those. Lower coverage, lower cost.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: Each affected PR has either (a) a recorded retro-review with findings logged, or (b) explicit waiver with rationale (low-risk doc/test change)
- SC2: Any critical or important finding from retro-review is filed as a bug ticket
- SC3: The 1624-5fb9 regression test in test-ci-llm-review-job.sh remains GREEN going forward (gate cannot reappear)
